summary: SPEC_DEFECT routing per Owner's five directions (1A-5A): amended T011/T012/T013 contracts, drafted new ADR-009 capturing the display / Decimal boundary, and added the ADR-009 row to docs/spec/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4. No code, tests, schemas, config or workflow state were modified.
rationale: The triage report at todo/triage/P01/T011/triage-001.json classifies this as SPEC_DEFECT because the Owner's five follow-up answers (1A 2A 3A 4A 5A) directly amend three frozen FROZEN_FROM_BASELINE_6C31778 contracts (T011, T012, T013) plus the spec catalogue, not the implementation. tools/workflow/core.py:1052-1058 routes SPEC_DEFECT to PLANNING, and the planner scope guard at core.py:1185-1187 restricts a SPEC_DEFECT planner to todo/phases/, todo/config.yaml (dependency fields), and docs/spec/. The Owner's decisions are mechanically derivable, so the planner is the correct role and outcome=PLAN_READY is the natural choice. Direction 1 / answer A removes the float API in src/robinhood_lp/protocol/ entirely (no rename-and-retype) and mandates a new ADR-009 under docs/spec/architecture/adr/; ADR-004 already established the two-domain policy but did not name the display-boundary module, so ADR-009 captures that explicit decision (single Decimal-typed helper to_display_price at the display boundary) and forbids float re-introduction without a stronger ADR. Direction 2 / answer A forces both roundUp=true and roundUp=false vectors for getAmount0Delta / getAmount1Delta, requires MathOracle.sol to expose a roundUp parameter, and forbids callers from adding 1 to a rounded-down result; the T012 contract now carries the per-direction vector requirement in Deliverables and Acceptance, and the no-1-add rule in Must-not. Direction 3 / answer A mandates pool_manager_address in PoolIdentity (composite record, never replacing the on-chain 32-byte PoolId) and uses ChainId(46630) as the cross-chain collision placeholder; the T011 contract now carries the composite identity in Outcome, Deliverables, Acceptance and Must-not, preserving V4's on-chain keccak256 PoolKey ABI-encoded PoolId while introducing a chain-agnostic record-level identity. Direction 4 / answer A replaces the existing 'at least one manually reviewed vector per edge class' language with a per-edge-class reviews block signed by git-author-commit or gpg; the T013 contract now names the reviews block fields, requires a CI test verifying the signature is not the candidate Developer, and forbids acceptance of self-attested review. Direction 5 / answer A mandates a new tests/test_oracle_drift.py that shells out to forge test --json and byte-compares against committed JSON, fails closed on any mismatch, and pytest.skips with an actionable message when forge is absent; the T013 contract now carries the drift-test specification in Deliverables and Acceptance, and forbids treating file-existence as a substitute for byte-comparison or treating a forge-absent environment as a passing test. All five Owner directions are addressed with mechanical, in-place edits to the four spec / contract files only; no src/, tests/, tools/oracle/, tools/workflow/, schemas, config, or evidence paths were touched. The pre-existing unverified implementation under src/ and tools/oracle/ is preserved untouched per WORKFLOW.md's pre-existing unverified implementation clause; the T012 attempt 2 Developer is responsible for the corresponding Python / Solidity source edits once plan-review approves. Task state remains PLANNING for T011 / T012 / T013; the controller / Manager handles the next transition.
